title: SAGA: A Memory-Efficient Accelerator for GANN Construction via Harnessing Vertex Similarity
problem: Graph-traversal-based Approximate Nearest Neighbor (GANN) construction faces severe memory bottlenecks due to high-dimensional vertices and dynamic graph updates. Existing accelerators like NDSearch struggle with the massive pre-processing overhead required for dynamic graph scenarios.
motivation: GANN construction is critical for recommendation systems and social networks, but memory-intensive vertex representations and dynamic updates make real-world deployment impractical.
method: SAGA groups vertices that have the same starting point during graph construction, reducing memory waste by storing similar data only once. It splits vertices into two types: 'key' vertices (primary references) and 'non-key' variants that store only small differences from their key vertex. Since these differences fall in a narrow range, they need fewer bits to represent, enabling mixed-precision quantization (using variable numbers of bits for different data). A specialized two-level hardware scheduler with a bit-serial mixed-precision unit executes this efficiently.
key_novelty: SAGA reduces memory bottlenecks in dynamic nearest-neighbor graph construction by grouping similar vertices to enable mixed-precision quantization (storing different data with different numbers of bits).
contributions: Novel similarity-based vertex clustering technique that minimizes detection overhead in dynamic graphs
Mixed-precision decomposition of vertices enabling lower bit-width quantization
Specialized two-level scheduling and bit-serial execution unit
9.30× speedup and 7.60× energy savings over NDSearch with retained accuracy

metrics.speedup: 9.30× over CPU, 4.87× over GPU, 4.15× over NDSearch
metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 35.46× over CPU, 7.60× over GPU, 5.15× over NDSearch

primary_theme: Memory-efficient graph-construction acceleration via vertex similarity and mixed-precision
